value.headline: One week into early voting, Ohio Democrats are outperforming Republicans
value.claim: ~230k cast: D 95k, U 67k, R 64k; at this point in 2024 R 36% / D 26%, now D 41% / R 28%; in Trump's 81 counties D 20/R 44 in 2024 vs 39/39 now
value.cmp: 2024 presidential year, same days-before-ED; party = primary-ballot affiliation
value.evidence: [M] SOS voter file, E-22: D 96,673 / U 69,201 / R 65,197 (D 41.8, R 28.2) - the snapshot holds. But by E-11 the D lead fell to D+4.8 (D 31.9 / R 27.1); Trump-won counties are R+7.8 at E-11 (D 26.0 / R 33.8), not tied. Same-person comparison: D affiliates at 85% of their 2024 same-day volume, R at 60%. 2022 party splits are not published, so the '2022' claim cannot be tested.

rows.source: News 5 Cleveland (Morgan Trau): One week into early voting, Ohio Democrats are outperforming Republicans
rows.note: The verdict is our like-for-like reading of the claim (grade I); the evidence cites its own grades.

value.headline: Early voting figures suggest Democratic gains in Ohio's most Trump-friendly counties
value.claim: Trump+20 counties: R lead over D 30 pts in 2024 -> 5 pts now; electorate ~27 pts more D than 2024 same point; Harris counties at 74% of 2024 turnout vs 67% in strongest Trump counties
value.cmp: 2024, same point; first ~5 days of voting
value.evidence: [M] At E-11, Trump+20 counties (72): R-D +13.7 vs +21.5 in 2024 (narrowed 7.8, not 25); statewide D-R swing 9.7 pts (2024 R+4.9 -> 2026 D+4.8), not 27; turnout ratio Harris-won 0.665 vs Trump+20 0.637 (2.8-pt gap, not 7). CNN itself said 'far from determinative' and 'very early' (11% of 2022 turnout).

rows.source: CNN: Early voting figures suggest Democratic gains in Ohio's most Trump-friendly coun
rows.note: The verdict is our like-for-like reading of the claim (grade I); the evidence cites its own grades.

value.evidence: [M] same test as CNN row; the gap in Trump+20 counties is +13.7 R at E-11; geography-weighted Trump margin of the early electorate is T+12.7 vs T+13.6 in 2024 same day (0.9 pt bluer).

rows.note: The verdict is our like-for-like reading of the claim (grade I); the evidence cites its own grades.

value.headline: Democrats lead early voting in Ohio

value.evidence: [M] numbers hold for E-22; the D-R lead decayed from D+14.2 (E-25) to D+4.8 (E-11) while 2024's stayed at R+5 throughout; the enthusiasm reading is partly supported (same-person D pace 85% of 2024 vs R 60%).

value.headline: Early in-person voting in Ohio nearly 4 times higher than 2022 midterm
value.evidence: [V] SOS releases: 194,841 (10/13/2026) vs 50,368 (10/18/2022); in-person really is ~4x, but mail requests fell (2026: 717k mail requests by 10/24 vs 2022: 940,160 by the 10/25 release). Total cast: 2026 1,003,351 at E-11 vs 2022 817,644 at E-7 -> ahead of 2022, but nowhere near 4x. A channel shift, not a 4x surge.
